title: Your Glow-Up Aura

plan.title: Your aura, before you say a word
How people read you (and get it wrong)
What your elements do to your face and fit
Your colours, worked out from your chart
You in rooms, photos and first meetings
Your glow-up, one month at a time
The small details that make it yours
When your aura dims, and the reset

strong.text:
Yeon: Strong chart. Your aura is turned up loud by default. People feel you before they see you.

Bom: That's presence. Not everyone has it.

Yeon: Not everyone has to stand next to it at a party, either.

Your glow-up isn't adding more. It's one soft thing that lets people in: a warmer colour near your face, a smile before you speak.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your aura is already at full volume. Find the dimmer.

weak.text:
Bom: Your chart runs soft. Your aura is gentle. People feel calm near you before they notice you.

Yeon: Which means they sometimes don't notice you. Rude of them. Also fixable.

Bom: Your glow-up is one strong anchor: a colour, a piece, a signature that says "I'm here".

Pick one thing people will remember you by and wear it on purpose for a month.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Soft auras glow with one strong anchor. Pick yours.

strong.text:
On a strong chart, the first read above lands faster and firmer than you intend. Whatever your style of confidence, it shows, and people can mistake it for judgment or impatience. The fix is tiny and physical. Smile with your eyes before you speak. Nod while people talk. Ask a second question before offering your view. These cues tell people your strength is on their side.

Also watch your resting face in photos and on video calls. Strong charts often look stern without meaning to, simply because they're concentrating. A softer jaw and slightly raised brows change the read completely. Practice once in a mirror. It feels silly for ten seconds and works for years.

One more cue: your pace. Strong charts walk and talk fast, which reads as busy and slightly unavailable. Slow down by ten percent when you enter a room and when you start a conversation. It costs you nothing and it makes you seem like a person with time for people, which is very attractive on a powerful person.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your concentrating face reads as 'you're fired.' Soften the jaw. It works.

weak.text:
On a weak chart, the first read above often comes with a softer layer on top, small protective habits that undersell you: shrinking posture on tired days, a hand covering your mouth when you laugh, sentences that end like questions. None of it is your personality. It's protection, and people read it as less than you are.

Try three small changes. Stand with your weight even on both feet. Finish sentences with a full stop in your voice. Let your laugh be visible. People will start reading the person you actually are, warm and interesting and more capable than the first ten seconds suggested.

One more cue: take the compliment. When someone says they like what you're wearing, the weak-chart reflex is to explain that it was cheap or old or borrowed. Say "thank you" and stop. Accepting a compliment reads as confidence, and people quietly recalibrate how they see you.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Full stop at the end of your sentences. People hear the real you.

strong.text:
A strong chart's style trap is repetition. You found what works and you wear it like a uniform, which is efficient and slightly armored. The fix is not abandoning your signature. It's rotating one element at a time: a new texture this month, a different shape next month, an unexpected accessory after that.

Also check that your clothes leave room for warmth. Strong charts tend to buy pieces that look capable. Add pieces that feel good to be near: soft knits, a relaxed fit, something people want to touch when they hug you. Approachable and powerful is the combination that makes a strong aura magnetic.

When you shop, ask one question before buying: does this make me look more approachable or more armored? Strong charts already have the armor. Spend on the approachable side, a knit that begs to be touched, a shirt with a little ease, shoes that make you walk more slowly. Your strength will still be obvious. It just won't be the only thing people see.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your uniform works. Rotate one piece a month so it stays a style, not armor.

weak.text:
A weak chart's style trap is invisibility. You buy what's safe, what's on sale, what your friend recommended, and your closet ends up full of clothes that belong to nobody in particular. The fix is choosing a few signature pieces and wearing them often, on purpose, until people associate them with you.

Also buy one thing this season purely because you love it. Not because it's practical or versatile. Weak charts rarely give themselves that permission. A single loved piece changes how you carry your whole body, and people notice the carrying more than the clothes.

When you shop, ask one question before buying: would I wear this if nobody I know would see it? If yes, it's yours. If you're only buying it because it seems safe or popular, put it back. A smaller wardrobe of clothes you actually love beats a full closet of compromises every time.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: One loved piece changes how you stand. Go find yours.

strong.text:
For a strong chart, the vibe shift is from impressive to inviting. You already have presence. What you're adding is ease: laughing at yourself, admitting what you don't know, letting someone else lead a conversation. Those moments make your strength feel safe to be around.

Try one experiment this month: in every social setting, find the quietest person and make them feel interesting for five minutes. Strong charts who do this become the person everyone wants to sit next to, which is a glow-up no outfit can match.

And let your face rest more. Strong charts often wear concentration as their default expression, which reads as intensity. A relaxed mouth and softer eyes when you're not talking tell people you're comfortable, and comfortable people are the easiest to approach.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Find the quietest person in the room. Make them feel interesting. Instant glow.

weak.text:
For a weak chart, the vibe shift is from pleasant to present. You're already kind and easy to be with. What you're adding is weight: saying what you think, taking a seat in the middle of the table, letting your opinions have a little edge.

Try one experiment this month: in every social setting, share one real opinion and hold it gently when someone disagrees. Not stubbornly, just without folding. Warmth plus a clear point of view is a combination people find hard to resist. That's the vibe you're growing into.

And let your posture take up the space it's entitled to. Shoulders back, feet planted, hands visible. It sounds like a posture lecture, and it is, but small changes in how you hold yourself change how people treat you within days.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Hold one opinion gently when someone disagrees. Don't fold. That's the vibe.

strong.text:
Strong charts dim through overuse. You keep pushing, keep leading, keep handling everything because you can, and the glow turns into strain. It shows in a tight jaw, clipped replies, clothes that get more severe as the stress rises.

Your recovery is release, not more discipline. Move your body hard, then rest it properly. Spend time where you're not in charge. Laugh at something stupid. Let your style relax for a weekend, comfortable pieces you still feel good in. The glow comes back when the force has somewhere to go.

A warning sign to watch: when you start dressing like you're going into battle on ordinary days, the strain is showing. That's the moment to cancel one thing and do something purely restorative, before the edge turns into exhaustion.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You dim from pushing. The fix is letting go, not trying harder.

weak.text:
Weak charts dim through depletion. You give and adapt and accommodate until there's nothing left, and the glow fades into tiredness. It shows in posture, in skipped routines, in the same comfortable clothes three days running because choosing anything else feels like effort.

Your recovery is refueling, not trying harder. Sleep, eat warm food, spend time with people who ask nothing of you. Keep one small grooming ritual even on bad days, the one that makes you feel like yourself. The glow returns when the tank fills, and it fills faster than you expect when you let it.

A warning sign to watch: when you skip that little ritual two days running, the tank is low. That's the moment to rest, not push. Treat it as a fuel gauge, not a failure.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You dim from running on empty. Refuel first. The glow comes back with it.

peer_strong.text: Your chart is heavy on {dm_el}, your own element. In style terms, that's an aura of pure self: consistent, confident, recognizable at a distance. The risk is a look that says only one thing, loudly, forever. More of your own element in your clothes would just repeat the message. That's why your palette leads with {helper_el}, the element your strength flows into. Let your home element live in small details and let the lead family do the talking. A practical test: lay out your five most-worn outfits. If they all say the same thing, swap one piece in each for something from your lead family.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: A chart full of you. Your outfit doesn't need to repeat the point.

output_strong.text: Your chart is heavy on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} produces, the family of expression and flair. Your aura already performs: big personality, strong taste, a look people comment on. The risk is too many statements at once. That's why your palette deliberately goes easy on {heavy_el} and leads with {helper_el} instead, giving all that expression a structure to sit in. One statement per outfit. Let the rest frame it. A practical test: before you leave the house, remove one accessory. It almost always improves the look.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Heavy {heavy_el}: you have five statements per outfit. Pick one.

wealth_strong.text: Your chart is heavy on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} manages. In style that shows up as a practical, put-together, slightly corporate aura: you look like you have a plan and a spreadsheet for it. The risk is looking capable and not much else. Your palette leads with {helper_el} to bring the expressive side forward. Add one detail purely for joy, an odd earring, a great sock, a pattern you'd never call sensible. A practical test: if every item you own has a practical justification, it's time for one that doesn't.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Heavy {heavy_el}: you look very capable. Add one detail just for joy.

power_strong.text: Your chart is heavy on {heavy_el}, the element that controls your {dm_el}, the family of rules and standards. Your aura reads as disciplined and correct, sometimes stiff, the person whose shoes are always clean. The risk is a look that seems to follow a dress code nobody else got. Your palette leads with {helper_el}, the element that classically eases pressure on a strong chart. Loosen one rule per outfit: a sleeve rolled, a button undone, a texture that relaxes the whole thing. A practical test: wear one piece slightly undone this week, a collar open, a sleeve pushed up, and notice who relaxes around you.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Heavy {heavy_el}: you dress like there's an inspection. Break one rule per outfit.

resource_strong.text: Your chart is heavy on {heavy_el}, the element that feeds your {dm_el}. That gives your aura a cushioned, comfortable quality, thoughtful, soft, a bit cocooned. Your style may lean cozy to the point of shapeless: layers, big knits, things that hide. Your palette goes easy on {heavy_el} for exactly that reason and leads with {helper_el}, which gives the comfort some direction. Keep the softness. Add one shape that shows where you are inside it. A practical test: replace one oversized layer with something that shows your shape, and see how differently people respond.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Heavy {heavy_el}: very cozy, slightly hidden. Add one shape that shows you.

output_weak.text: Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} produces. On a weak chart, expression drains rather than shines: you put lots of effort into looking good for others and end up tired of the effort. Your look may swing between trying too hard and giving up. Your palette leads with {helper_el} to refill rather than perform. Choose fewer, better pieces that look good without daily work. A practical test: choose an outfit you can put on in two minutes and still feel good in. Make it your default on tired days.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Leaning {heavy_el}: you try so hard to look good. Fewer pieces, less effort, more you.

wealth_weak.text: Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} manages. On a weak chart that shows up as a style built around other people's needs: practical bags, clothes for every errand, nothing that's just for you. Your aura reads as helpful and tired. Your palette leads with {helper_el} to give you support instead of more duties. Edit your wardrobe down so it serves you, not your schedule. A practical test: empty your bag. Take out everything that's there for someone else. Notice how much lighter you feel.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Leaning {heavy_el}: your clothes are for errands. Buy one thing for you.

power_weak.text: Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element that controls your {dm_el}. On a weak chart, that pressure shows up as dressing to avoid judgment: safe, correct, nothing anyone could criticize. Your aura reads as careful. Your palette leads with {helper_el} for support and keeps {heavy_el} colors to small accents. Choose one piece a week that you'd wear if nobody were grading you. A practical test: wear something you love to a place where you usually dress safely. Nothing bad happens. That's the point.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Leaning {heavy_el}: you dress so nobody can criticize. Wear one ungraded piece a week.

rooted_on_paper.text: In style terms, that gap reads as a look that seems confident in photos and feels shaky in person, or the reverse. Your palette is picked to give you the root your chart lacks, through {helper_el}, so wear the lead family on the days you feel least sure. It does more than you'd think. A practical test: on the next uncertain morning, reach for your lead family first and notice whether the day feels steadier.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Wear your lead colors on wobbly days. They're picked to steady you.

output_strong.text: {miss_el} is missing from your visible pillars, and for your {dm_el} it's the output element, expression. A strong chart without it can look powerful but closed, all substance and no signal. This is exactly why {miss_el} leads your palette: wearing it is the simplest way to borrow the missing element and let some of your personality out. Start with one expressive piece per outfit and let it carry your personality.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: No {miss_el} in your pillars, so it leads your colors. Borrow it.

wealth_strong.text: {miss_el} is missing from your visible pillars, and for your {dm_el} it's the wealth element, the practical, finished side of life. A strong chart without it can look stylish but unfinished: great ideas, loose ends, a hem that's been coming down for months. Borrow it through finish: tailoring, repairs done, shoes cared for. Finish is the most underrated glow-up there is.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: No {miss_el}: great taste, loose hems. Get the repairs done.

power_strong.text: {miss_el} is missing from your visible pillars, and for your {dm_el} it's the power element, structure and rules. A strong chart without it dresses entirely on instinct, which can be brilliant or chaotic. Borrow some structure: a few rules for yourself, one silhouette that always works, a short list of what you do and don't buy. Three rules are plenty. More than that is a uniform.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: No {miss_el}: you dress on pure instinct. Write three style rules.

resource_strong.text: {miss_el} is missing from your visible pillars, and for your {dm_el} it's the resource element, comfort and care. A strong chart without it often neglects itself: no skincare routine, clothes chosen in a rush, sleep last on the list. You don't need it in your colors. Borrow it as care instead: a nightly routine and clothes that feel good, not just look right. Care shows on the face faster than any purchase.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: No {miss_el}: you never look after yourself. Borrow it as care, not color.

output_weak.text: {miss_el} is missing from your visible pillars, and for your {dm_el} it's the output element, expression. On a weak chart that keeps you from overspending your energy on appearances, which is protective. Don't chase it through bold looks. Let it show in one small, personal detail instead. Small and personal beats bold and borrowed.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: No {miss_el}: you don't need a bold look. One personal detail is enough.

wealth_weak.text: {miss_el} is missing from your visible pillars, and for your {dm_el} it's the wealth element, the practical side. On a weak chart that's less to carry, though you may not care much about upkeep. Keep it light: a few quality basics you look after, so your look holds up without effort. Low effort, good quality, kept well. That's the formula.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: No {miss_el}: you ignore upkeep. Three good basics, cared for. Done.

power_weak.text: {miss_el} is missing from your visible pillars, and for your {dm_el} it's the power element, outside pressure. On a weak chart that's a relief, and your palette keeps it to accents anyway. Just give yourself one gentle structure, like a weekly outfit plan, so your style doesn't drift. Structure that you choose feels like support, not pressure.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: No {miss_el}: good, less pressure. One gentle routine keeps you on track.

resource_weak.text: {miss_el} is missing from your visible pillars, and for your {dm_el} it's the resource element, the one that feeds you. That's the core reason {miss_el} leads your palette: wearing it brings in what your chart doesn't supply. Pair it with real care, rest and comfort, and your aura fills out fast. Comfort and color together do more than either alone.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: No {miss_el}, the element that feeds you. That's why it leads your colors.

none_strong.text: All five elements show up somewhere in your pillars, even if some only as hidden stems. On a strong chart that gives you range: you can pull off almost any look. The risk is wearing all of it at once. Choose one direction per outfit, led by your palette, and let the range show over a week rather than in one mirror. Range is a gift when it's edited.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: All five elements: you can wear anything. Not everything at once.

none_weak.text: All five elements show up somewhere in your pillars, even if some only as hidden stems. On a weak chart that means many styles suit you, but you may not trust any of them. Start with your palette's lead family and wear it until it feels like yours. Confidence comes from repetition, not variety. Repeat a look you love until it feels like home.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Many looks suit you. Pick your lead colors and repeat them until they're yours.

output.text:
Here is how your colors are worked out, {dm_short}. Your chart is strong, so it already carries plenty of your home element, {dm_el}, and the element that feeds it. More of either would only turn the volume up. Saju balances a strong chart by giving its strength somewhere to go, and for you that is {helper_el}, which your {dm_el} generates. That makes {helper_el} your lead color family: the backbone of your wardrobe, the colors you reach for first. Your home colors stay, but as base notes rather than the headline. Go easy on {easy_el} colors, the element that feeds you: your chart has enough of that support already, so keep it to small accents.

To start, add one piece from your lead family this week and wear it close to your face. Then look at photos from that day. Most strong charts are surprised by how much more relaxed they look.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Strong chart, so your lead colors balance you: {helper_el}. Not more of the same.

wealth.text:
Here is how your colors are worked out, {dm_short}. Your chart is strong, and it already pours a lot of energy outward through {easy_el}, the expressive element born from your {dm_el}. That's why the usual balancing color for a strong chart isn't your lead. It's already your heaviest element. Instead your lead is {helper_el}, the element your Day Master works on and shapes. It gives all that strength something concrete to hold. Make {helper_el} the backbone of your wardrobe, and go easy on {easy_el} colors, keeping them to small accents, because more of them would only pile onto what you already have plenty of.

To start, add one piece from your lead family this week, something with substance, a coat, a knit, a pair of boots. It anchors your look the way a plan anchors your energy.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your lead colors are {helper_el}. They give your strength something to hold.

resource.text:
Here is how your colors are worked out, {dm_short}. Your chart is weak, so the colors that help you most are support, not balance. Saju strengthens a weak Day Master with the element that feeds it, and for your {dm_el} that is {helper_el}. That makes {helper_el} your lead color family: wear it generously, close to your face, on the days you need to feel more like yourself. Your own element's colors are your second family, a quiet backup. Go easy on {easy_el} colors, the element that pressures your Day Master: on a chart that needs support, too much of it weighs you down. Keep it to small accents.

To start, wear one piece from your lead family on the next day you feel low. Notice whether you stand differently. Support often shows up in posture before it shows up in mood.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Weak chart, so your lead colors feed you: {helper_el}. Wear them generously.

peer.text:
Here is how your colors are worked out, {dm_short}. Your chart is weak, but it already holds plenty of the element that feeds you, {heavy_el}. More of that wouldn't add root, only weight. What steadies you best is your own element, {helper_el}, worn with confidence. That makes {helper_el} your lead color family: the colors that make you look most like yourself. Go easy on {easy_el} colors, the element that pressures your Day Master, because on a weak chart it weighs rather than polishes. Keep them to small accents.

To start, wear your lead family on an ordinary day, not a special one. The point is to feel like yourself on a Tuesday, not only at events.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your lead colors are your own: {helper_el}. Wear them like you mean it.

wood.text:
Your {helper_el} family: forest green, sage, olive, moss and deep teal. Natural textures belong here too, linen, cotton, raw wood, woven straw, botanical prints. Start with one green piece near your face, a knit, a shirt, a scarf, and build around it. A simple formula that works almost anywhere: one {helper_el} color on top, a neutral below, one natural texture. Green suits growth, and it makes you look fresh and alive rather than loud.

Three outfit formulas built on your lead family. Work: a sage or olive knit, tailored trousers, clean leather shoes. Date: a deep green shirt or top, something soft below, one natural-texture accessory. Weekend: a linen overshirt in moss, relaxed denim, good walking shoes. In each, the green sits closest to your face. That's where it does the most work.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Lead with greens: forest, sage, olive, moss. Plus linen and natural textures.

fire.text:
Your {helper_el} family: coral, rust, warm red, terracotta, berry and soft pink. Warm metals and a bit of sheen belong here too, satin, a glossy finish, a warm-toned watch. Start with one warm color near your face, a top, a scarf, a lip or a bolder watch strap, and build around it. A simple formula: one {helper_el} color as the focus, everything else quiet. Warm colors bring color to your face and warmth to your presence, which is exactly the job they have in your chart.

Three outfit formulas built on your lead family. Work: a rust or terracotta top under a simple jacket. Date: a warm red or berry piece with a little sheen, everything else calm. Weekend: a coral tee or sweater, easy trousers, a warm-toned watch. In each, the warm color sits near your face, where it brings color to your skin.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Lead with warm colors: coral, rust, warm red, berry. A little sheen too.

earth.text:
Your {helper_el} family: camel, sand, ochre, mustard, oatmeal and warm brown. Soft structured textures belong here, suede, brushed wool, chunky knits, leather with a matte finish. Start with one earth-toned layer, a coat, a cardigan, a pair of good boots, and build around it. A simple formula: one {helper_el} piece with weight to it, one lighter layer, nothing fussy. These colors make you look grounded and expensive at the same time.

Three outfit formulas built on your lead family. Work: a camel blazer or cardigan over a simple top. Date: an ochre or mustard knit with dark trousers and suede shoes. Weekend: an oatmeal sweater, relaxed trousers, sturdy boots. In each, the earth tone carries the outfit's weight: outerwear, knitwear or footwear.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Lead with earth tones: camel, sand, ochre, oatmeal. Suede and good wool.

metal.text:
Your {helper_el} family: crisp white, ivory, silver, dove gray and pewter. Clean structure belongs here too, a sharp collar, a well-cut blazer, polished metal jewelry. Start with one white or gray piece with a clean line and build around it. A simple formula: one {helper_el} piece, one strong shape, one metal accessory you wear every day. These colors give you clarity and finish, which is the job they have in your chart.

Three outfit formulas built on your lead family. Work: a crisp white shirt, a sharp jacket, one metal accessory. Date: ivory or dove gray in a fluid fabric, with polished shoes. Weekend: a gray knit, clean sneakers, a simple silver ring or chain. In each, the light, clean color sits where people look first.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Lead with white, ivory, silver, dove gray. Clean lines, one metal piece.

water.text:
Your {helper_el} family: navy, ink, deep blue, black and midnight. Fluid fabrics belong here too, silk, soft jersey, anything with drape. Start with one deep blue or black piece that moves when you move, and build around it. A simple formula: one {helper_el} base, one fluid fabric, one point of light like a ring or a bright eye. These colors add depth and calm, and on you they read as composed rather than gloomy.

Three outfit formulas built on your lead family. Work: a navy jacket or knit with a softer layer underneath. Date: a black or ink piece in silk or soft jersey, one point of light near your face. Weekend: a deep blue overshirt, relaxed trousers, comfortable shoes. In each, the deep color forms the base, so your face and hands become the light.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Lead with navy, ink, deep blue, black. Fabrics that move with you.

second.wood: Your second family is {second_el}: greens and natural textures, worked in as a supporting layer rather than the main event.
second.fire: Your second family is {second_el}: warm colors like coral or rust, used as a supporting accent rather than the whole outfit.
second.earth: Your second family is {second_el}: camel, sand and oatmeal, perfect for the layer that ties a look together.
second.metal: Your second family is {second_el}: white, ivory and soft gray, best as the clean layer underneath.
second.water: Your second family is {second_el}: navy and deep blue, best as a calm base or one fluid piece.

easy.wood: In practice, going easy on {easy_el} means greens as a detail, a plant-print scarf or a single ring, not head to toe.
easy.fire: In practice, going easy on {easy_el} means warm reds and corals as a detail, a lip, a pocket square, a phone case, not the whole look.
easy.earth: In practice, going easy on {easy_el} means camel and brown as a detail, a belt or a bag, not a full outfit of them.
easy.metal: In practice, going easy on {easy_el} means white and gray as a detail, a collar or a watch, not a whole monochrome look.
easy.water: In practice, going easy on {easy_el} means navy and black as a detail, a pair of shoes or a slim belt, not an all-dark uniform.

rat.text: The branch under your Day Master shows the you people meet up close, at home, in a partner's eyes. Yours is the Rat, 子, deep winter Water and one of the four peach-blossom branches classical readers link with charm. Up close you're quick, witty and a little secretive, more magnetic at night than at noon. Your style tip from the Rat: keep one private detail that only people close to you notice, a lining, a tattoo, a bracelet under the sleeve. Intrigue suits you. Yours is also a peach-blossom branch, the one classical readers tie to natural charm. You don't need to try hard to be noticed. Your glow-up is choosing what you want to be noticed for.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Rat day branch: one secret detail only close people notice. Very you.

ox.text: The branch under your Day Master shows the you people meet up close. Yours is the Ox, 丑, cold wet Earth that stores Metal. Up close you're steady, loyal and slow to change, and your style can be the same: reliable to the point of stuck. The Ox's style tip: invest in a few things that last decades, then refresh one small element a season so the reliability looks chosen, not frozen. Yours is also a storehouse branch, linked with a private, reflective streak. Keep one beautiful thing that's just for you, worn under a layer or kept in a pocket. It shows in how you carry yourself.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Ox day branch: same look for a decade. Refresh one small thing a season.

tiger.text: The branch under your Day Master shows the you people meet up close. Yours is the Tiger, 寅, early-spring Wood with Fire inside, one of the travel branches. Up close you're bold, restless and protective. Your style should move with you: pieces that work on the go, a bag that's ready for a spontaneous trip, shoes you can walk all day in and still look sharp. Yours is also a travel branch, yeokma, the moving horse. Your look works best when it moves with you: pieces that travel, layer and survive a long day without wilting.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Tiger day branch: dress for the spontaneous trip. Always ready to go.

rabbit.text: The branch under your Day Master shows the you people meet up close. Yours is the Rabbit, 卯, pure spring Wood, a peach-blossom branch. Up close you're gentle, stylish and attentive to beauty in small things. Your style tip: soft textures, delicate details and a home that looks like your outfits. People notice the coherence and read it as taste, because it is. Yours is also a peach-blossom branch, the one classical readers tie to natural charm. You don't need to try hard to be noticed. Your glow-up is choosing what you want to be noticed for.

panel.speaker: bom

byeong-fire.aura:
Your aura is the sun: bright, warm, wide open. People feel invited the second you smile.

Bom: You make everyone feel like they're at the party.

Yeon: You also turn up looking like the party. Sometimes the room wanted a quieter guest.

Bom: Your glow-up is contrast. One calm, simple piece makes all that light look intentional.
byeong-fire.how-people-read-you: In the first ten seconds: confident, fun, easy to approach, maybe a little loud. People assume you're an extrovert with a hundred friends, and they're not entirely wrong. They feel included around you, which is a rare gift. The misreading comes from that same brightness. Some people think you're shallow because you're so cheerful, or that you need attention because you're so visible. They don't see how much you actually care, or how hurt you get when your effort goes unnoticed. To be read more fully, let a little quiet into your presence. Listen for longer. Share one serious thought among the jokes. Your sunny aura doesn't need dimming. It just becomes more trustworthy when people see that it's real all the way through.
byeong-fire.style: You look your best in clothes that feel open and bright. Clean, confident shapes that show your face and posture, short sleeves or rolled cuffs, shirts with an open collar, one piece with a bit of shine. You suit crisp fabrics and anything that catches light. The trap is wearing every statement at once, so the outfit competes with your personality instead of framing it. Pick one focal point per look and let the rest stay simple. Grooming that suits you is healthy and lively: a haircut with lift, skin that looks like it's seen the sun, a big smile you don't ration. In photos, face the light directly and laugh mid-shot. Posed doesn't suit you. Caught in the moment does.
byeong-fire.vibe: The glow-up you're after is the warm host with depth. Imagine the K-drama character who's the life of every party, then one quiet episode reveals how much they've been holding together for everyone. That depth is your new layer. Try a few shifts. Spend some time listening instead of telling. Keep one plan small and intimate instead of big and public. Post fewer stories and more meaningful moments. Let one close friend see you on a cloudy day. None of this makes you less fun. It makes your fun feel safe to be around. People trust a sun that also knows how to set. You'll notice your aura reading as warmer, more grown-up and much more magnetic.
byeong-fire.aura-dims: You lose your glow when you're running on empty but still performing. You keep showing up, smiling and making the jokes, but there's a flatness behind it that close friends notice. Your outfits might get louder to compensate, or you might stop caring and fall into the same tired hoodie for days. Either way, the fire is flickering. The reset is genuine joy, not performed joy. Dance in your room to embarrassing music. Spend time in actual sunlight, outdoors, without your phone. Do something creative where no one's watching, cook a ridiculous meal, paint badly, sing loudly. Say no to one social plan and don't explain. Rest isn't the opposite of shining. It's what makes tomorrow's sunrise possible.
byeong-fire.palette-intro: Your home element is Fire, {dm_short}, so the classic colors of your Day Master are the bright warm tones of the sun: coral, warm red, a glowing orange. They will always feel natural on you. How much of them you wear depends on your chart's balance, which the rest of this chapter works out.

spring.intro: The sun, born in spring. Everything was feeding you: new leaves, longer days, people who wanted your attention. So you grew up assuming warmth is normal. When someone's cold to you, it genuinely confuses you.

autumn.intro: An autumn sun. Lower in the sky, aimed at things: harvest, goals, results. You're warm, but you're also counting. You notice exactly who showed up for you and who just liked the post.

winter.intro: A winter sun. Short days, cold air, people who needed you more than they could give back. It made you tough and a little performative: the brightest one in the room, even on the days you're running on fumes.

earth.intro: Born in the between-season weeks, when Earth runs things. For the sun, that means everything you give turns into something solid: a friend's confidence, a plan that worked, a party you made happen. You're a great investment. Ask what you're getting back.

byeong-fire.strong: A strong {dm} chart is a fire with plenty of fuel. You radiate charisma and you're used to being noticed, so your look can turn into a performance: one statement too many, a volume that fills the room before you've spoken. The blind spot is heat without rest. Your glow-up is balance: some calm and contrast so the warmth reads as inviting rather than intense. Your palette leans on balancing elements for exactly that reason. In practice: keep the warmth, lose one statement per outfit, and let calm pieces frame your face. Your best photos will be the calm ones, when the warmth glows instead of blazes.
byeong-fire.weak: A weak {dm} chart is a flame in a drafty room. You have warmth and depth but often hide them in safe, unremarkable clothes chosen so nobody looks twice. The blind spot is dimming yourself before anyone asks. Your glow-up is fuel: comfort, confidence and one element in every look that's unmistakably you. Your palette leans on what feeds your fire. In practice: one warm, confident piece near your face every day is the quickest way to turn your flame back up. Your best photos will be the ones with real light on your face and real joy behind it.

presence.text:
The temperature changes when you arrive, Byeong. People turn toward you like a window in winter. You fill space easily, which is magnetic at parties and occasionally overwhelming in small meetings. In photos you look best laughing in real light, not posed. At first meetings, your strength is instant warmth. Your upgrade is depth on demand: after the first bright minutes, ask one serious question and listen fully. People will remember you as the fun one who also really saw them.

For video calls, face the window, turn the camera on early and greet people by name. Your warmth translates through a screen better than most people's.

Your K-drama character, Byeong: the sunny best friend who becomes the lead when the audience realizes they're the heart of the show. Big laugh, bright energy, one private scene where they cry alone. Let the other characters see that scene sometimes.

details.text: One bold accessory per look is your rule, Byeong: big earrings, a chunky ring, a watch with presence, sunglasses with personality. Fire loves light, so anything that catches it suits you, polished metal, glossy leather, a little shimmer. Your scent should be warm and bright, citrus or amber. Hair: volume and shine, a cut with lift. Teeth and smile matter more for you than for most: your laugh is your best accessory, so look after it and use it often. One rule worth keeping: if it catches the light, it belongs near your face.

one-month.heading: Your one-month glow-up
one-month.text: Your one-month glow-up, Byeong. Week one: sleep before midnight four nights out of seven. Week two: edit every outfit down to one statement. Week three: host something small and let other people shine at it. Week four: take a quiet day alone with no audience and nothing to post. You'll come back brighter, because the sun needs a night too.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Byeong, sleep before midnight. Even the sun clocks out.

three-words.heading: Your aura in three words, plus its evil twin
three-words.text:
Good days: radiant, generous, magnetic.

Tired days: loud, scattered, performing.

Yeon: "Performing" is when you're bright for them, not for you. People can feel the difference.

On flat days, don't force the shine. A quiet outfit and a real smile beat a forced sparkle.

reset.heading: Your reset kit
reset.text: Your reset kit, Byeong: two early nights, sunlight on your face first thing, a friend who makes you laugh, and one day with nothing to post. The sun recovers by setting properly.

occasions.heading: Three occasions, sorted
occasions.text: Three occasions, Byeong. Interview: one confident piece and everything else calm, so they remember you, not your outfit. First date: something that shows your face and your laugh. Wedding guest: a bit of shine, a lot of joy, one statement only. In all three, rest the night before. Your face does the rest.

glance.heading: First glance versus the truth
glance.text: First glance versus the truth, Byeong. They think: fun, loud, maybe a bit much. The truth: generous, thoughtful and more sensitive than your volume suggests. Close the gap with one quiet, attentive moment early on.

byeong-fire.title: You don't have an indoor voice. You have a stage voice and a smaller stage voice.
byeong-fire.text:
You light up rooms. Your laugh carries. People find you in a crowd without trying because you're the brightest thing in it.

Bom: Your warmth is visible.

Yeon: Your warmth is visible from space. Let's talk about when to dim it.
byeong-fire.end: Yeon: Next page: your aura, plus the moment it tips from "glowing" into "a lot".
